_doc: Parkway trees READ OFF PICTURES for the 1904 scene (T-1934). Hand-authored INPUT to tools/plant_prairie_1904_street_trees.py: on each stretch below, the rule's trees are withdrawn and these are planted in their place, each at a distance along the face's parkway line (the same line, 62 % of the way from the walk to the curb, that the rule plants on; at_m from the face's first point, as data/street_trees/1904.json measures it). A stretch is the run of the parkway the named pictures see, so an empty stretch is a reading too: the pictures show no tree there. Each reading is the trunk's x in the picture, carried to the parkway line through that picture's solved camera (data/reference_views/). docs/LIBERTIES.md L-pullman-18th-street-trees-1934 says what is read and what is chosen.

detroit_4a08065.date: 1897-1901 (the Detroit Photographic Co. imprint; the holder's 1890-1901)

seen_by: detroit_4a08065 x 43-570 (the Prairie front, squarely, from 228.5 m to the corner's bed)
stretches.note: Prairie Avenue's east parkway before the Pullman house, from its north end to the 18th Street corner's curbed bed (T-1881). The Detroit print sees the Prairie front squarely and governs along it (the large dormer and the stair land within a few px through its camera); each trunk's x is carried to the planting line (u 48.0 in the house's frame) through it. The 1890 Albertype plate (library image a16-albertype-1890-pullman-residence, no source record yet, so a check and not a reading) shows the same two trunks before the portico and at the corner, braced as young trees, at 248.0 and 257.2 m through its camera, 1.6 and 1.2 m south of the Detroit readings (toward 18th Street): the same 1 m or so its camera draws the front's dormer off along this face. Taylor's no. 1445 sees only the corner end, edge-on, and draws no trunk there; it is the earlier picture. The corner itself (257.5 m to the face's end) is not part of this stretch: the Detroit print's trunk at x 630 stands there on neither planting line through its camera, the stretch where it and Taylor's disagree (the corner's tree on 18th Street, T-1881), and the rule plants nothing within 10.5 m of the corner.

The rule stood a grown elm at 19.4 m, which drew through 16554's camera at x 1091 as a thick forked trunk against the stable's stack, where the print shows the stack and the sky clear; the print's one trunk on this stretch stands at x 996-1006, its foot at y 589 on the walk's far edge (this camera reads the parkway's feet about 5 px under the line's, as it does on Calumet's west parkway), 10 px across at about 41 m (about 0.35 m), behind the leader of the young tree at 248.8 m on the near parkway. The Detroit print of c. 1897-1901 sees this stretch at 115 m (x 902-941): a trunk rises behind the Fort Dearborn monument at x about 922, its foot hidden by the monument, so it cannot be put on this parkway or the lot behind it, and is a check, not a reading.

stretches.note: Calumet Avenue's west parkway north of the glasshouse ground's gate, curving into 18th Street opposite the Pullman stable (T-1934). Taylor's no. 16554 stood on the lawn inside its coping, a few metres from this walk, and its camera, re-solved with this corner's coping, the walk's outer edge and the stable's wall foot in its fit, sees the parkway at 15-30 m: each trunk's x is carried to the planting line through it, and its foot reads within 5-14 px of the line's (nearer the walk for the nearest). The rule stood three elms here, at 241.9, 250.9 and 259.9 m; the print shows three young trees, two close together before the walk's turn. The rule's tree at 241.9 m stood just past the print's edge, but its trunk drew inside the frame at x 1155-1175, where the print shows grass, so it is withdrawn too.
